messages.content: 你能計算從地球到一個新發現的距離為4.22光年的外行星，再到另一個距離第一顆外行星6.1光年的外行星，最後再回到距離第二顆外行星5.88光年的地球所需的時間嗎？假設真空中光的速度為299792458公尺/秒。

function.name: light_travel_time
function.description: Calculate the time taken for light to travel from a celestial body to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

distance_in_light_years.description: The distance between the two celestial bodies in light years. This is a float type value.

speed_of_light.description: The speed of light in vacuum, in m/s. Default value is 299792458 m/s.

message.reasoning: We need to compute total travel time: Earth to first exoplanet (4.22 ly), then to second exoplanet (distance between them? It says "another exoplanet at distance 6.1 light-years from the first exoplanet". So distance between them is 6.1 ly). Then back to Earth from second exoplanet at distance 5.88 ly. So total distance = 4.22 + 6.1 + 5.88 = 16.2 ly. Compute time: 16.2 light-years / speed of light. Light-year is distance light travels in one year. So 1 ly = c * 1 year. So time in years = total distance in ly = 16.2 years. But they want time in maybe seconds? They gave speed of light in m/s. We can compute seconds: 1 year = 365.25 days * 24h * 3600s = 31557600 s. So 16.2 years = 16.2 * 31557600 = about 511,? Let's compute: 31557600*16 = 504921600; plus 0.2*31557600=6311520; sum=511,? 504,921,600+6,311,520=511,233,120 s. So ~5.112e8 seconds. Alternatively compute using function: distance in light years 16.2, speed of light 299792458 m/s. But function expects distance in light years and speed of light. It will compute time? The function likely returns time in seconds? We need to call function. Provide distance 16.2. Let's call.
